newsitem.title: ITALY: New talks called in Italy metalworkers' dispute.
newsitem.headline: New talks called in Italy metalworkers' dispute.

text.p: Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu called fresh talks with unions and management for later on Tuesday in a bid to end the long-running dispute which has afflicted the metalworkers' and engineering sector.

Treu held separate talks with the two sides earlier on Tuesday and called a new round of negotiations, again to be held separately, for 2000 GMT, the director general of the association of metalworkers' employers, Michele Figurati, said.
"This evening we will see if we are about to enter the concluding phase," said Gianni Italia, head of the FIM union.

Unions representing 1.7 million workers in the metalworkers and engineering sector, which accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy, are locked in dispute with management over pay increases for the 1996-1998 period.
Unions want full compensation for an overshoot in inflation in the past contract period and have already called two one-day strikes to press home their demands.

Management say they cannot afford the wage claim. A number of other sectors are awaiting the outcome of the dispute before concluding their own deals. Analysts are anxious that if union demands are met in full, inflation might be forced higher. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
